context_label: Definitive treatment of locally advanced cervical cancer
title: Pembrolizumab with cisplatin and radiotherapy for cervical cancer
schedule_label: Cycles 1–5 last 21 days. Cisplatin is planned weekly for five doses in cycles 1–2, with a possible sixth dose. Pembrolizumab continues alone from cycle 3 and changes to every 42 days for cycles 6–20. Treatment can end earlier and lasts up to 24 months.
schedule_summary: Cycles 1–5 last 21 days. Cisplatin is planned weekly for five doses in cycles 1–2, with a possible sixth dose. Pembrolizumab continues alone from cycle 3 and changes to every 42 days for cycles 6–20. Treatment can end earlier and lasts up to 24 months.
purpose: The aim is to cure the cancer. Radiation treats the cervix and nearby areas. Cisplatin helps radiation work, and pembrolizumab helps the immune system recognise cancer cells.
indication_text: Adults with FIGO 2014 stage III–IVA cervical cancer who have not had definitive treatment. PD-L1 testing is not required for this indication.
administration_text: When both drugs are due, pembrolizumab is infused over 30 minutes before cisplatin over 60 minutes. IV fluids protect the kidneys. Radiation follows cisplatin that day. External-beam radiation and the later internal treatment (brachytherapy) use a separately booked calendar.
monitoring_summary: Blood count, kidney and liver tests and glucose before each cycle. Thyroid tests every 3–6 weeks, cortisol and hearing checks when indicated. Cisplatin visits need hydration and electrolyte review.
review_status: Independent oncology, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Pembrolizumab
agents.explanation: Blocks a signal that normally slows immune cells. This can help them attack the cancer. The same response can inflame healthy organs.
agents.mechanism: Blocks a signal that normally slows immune cells. This can help them attack the cancer. The same response can inflame healthy organs.
agents.watch: Report a new cough, breathlessness, diarrhoea, rash, severe fatigue, thirst or dizziness, including after your last dose. Carry your immunotherapy alert card.
risks: Inflammation of lungs, bowel, liver or kidneys
symptoms: Inflammation of lungs, bowel, liver or kidneys
visual: Blocks a signal that normally slows immune cells. This can help them attack the cancer. The same response can inflame healthy organs.

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.explanation: Attaches to DNA so cells struggle to copy and repair it. During radiotherapy this can increase damage to the cancer cells.
agents.mechanism: Attaches to DNA so cells struggle to copy and repair it. During radiotherapy this can increase damage to the cancer cells.
agents.watch: Call if you pass much less urine, cannot keep fluids down, or develop ringing ears, hearing changes or persistent tingling.

common_effects.title: What you may notice
common_effects.text: Fatigue, nausea or appetite changes can build during pelvic treatment. The team can help with food, fluids and bowel symptoms.

serious_effects.title: Inflamed lungs · Pembrolizumab
serious_effects.text: Call urgently for a new cough or breathlessness.

serious_effects.title: Diarrhoea or pelvic symptoms · Pembrolizumab and pelvic radiation
serious_effects.text: Phone about diarrhoea, severe pain, heavy bleeding or changes in passing urine. The cause needs assessment.

serious_effects.title: Kidney or salt changes · Cisplatin and pembrolizumab
serious_effects.text: Call if you pass very little urine, vomit repeatedly or cannot drink.

serious_effects.title: Ringing or hearing loss · Cisplatin
serious_effects.text: Report changes before your next infusion.

serious_effects.title: Hormone changes · Pembrolizumab
serious_effects.text: New dizziness, unusual thirst or severe fatigue needs same-day assessment.

questions.q: What if my radiation is cancelled?
questions.a: Phone both teams. Cisplatin waits until radiation resumes. Your team separately decides whether pembrolizumab is due.

questions.q: What happens after the fifth week?
questions.a: The team checks whether a sixth cisplatin dose is appropriate. Pembrolizumab continues on its own. Ask for the dates for brachytherapy and the switch to six-weekly visits.

support.title: Getting help
support.text: Call the 24-hour oncology line for fever or shaking chills, new breathlessness, frequent diarrhoea, very little urine, severe headache, heavy bleeding or severe weakness. If breathing becomes difficult at rest, seek emergency help.

teachback: What if my radiation is cancelled? Show where you will find your 24-hour contact number.
consent_support: Discuss cure intent, fertility before pelvic radiation, early menopause, vaginal narrowing and sexual health, hearing and kidney injury, and immune effects that may persist or need hormone replacement.
safety_note: Call the 24-hour oncology line for fever or shaking chills, new breathlessness, frequent diarrhoea, very little urine, severe headache, heavy bleeding or severe weakness. If breathing becomes difficult at rest, seek emergency help.

evidence.title: KEYNOTE-A18 · stage III–IVA subgroup
evidence.interpretation: Among people with stage III–IVA disease, the group receiving immunotherapy with chemoradiation had fewer deaths during follow-up.
evidence.limitations: Subgroup findings are exploratory. The overall trial also included earlier node-positive stages. It did not test pembrolizumab alone against chemoradiotherapy or directly compare induction chemotherapy.

monitoring_schedule.title: Tests and timing

rows.label: Before starting
cells: Blood count, kidney and liver tests, blood sugar and thyroid tests. Hearing assessment if indicated.
Tell the team about hearing loss, immune disease, steroid use or problems drinking.

rows.label: Before and during cycles
cells: Blood count, kidney and liver tests and glucose before each cycle. Thyroid tests every 3–6 weeks, cortisol and hearing checks when indicated. Cisplatin visits need hydration and electrolyte review.
Report less urine, diarrhoea, cough, marked fatigue or dizziness. Give the team the actual radiation dates.

rows.label: After radiation and immunotherapy
cells: The team reviews pelvic recovery, cancer response and delayed immune effects.
Keep the alert card. Ask when to return for bleeding, bowel or bladder problems, vaginal changes or menopause symptoms.

monitoring_schedule.note: The team individualises response assessments and extra tests according to symptoms and treatment aim.

prescription_phases.label: Cycles 1 and 2 · day 1

medicines.name: Metoclopramide
medicines.timing: Up to three times daily · Subsequent days / as directed
medicines.note: Leave at least 6 hours between doses. Maximum 5 days and 30 mg/day or 0.5 mg/kg/day, whichever is lower. Review extrapyramidal risk with olanzapine.

additional_support: Use the dated anti-sickness prescription for the scheduled platinum treatment. Ask which dose to take next and how to use rescue medicine.
prescription_notes: Confirm radiotherapy delivery and review fluids, kidney tests, steroids and home anti-sickness doses.
